usageNotes: Use this to audit or inventory all API tokens associated with a given PDM user before rotating credentials, diagnosing auth failures, or verifying token expiry. Callers need either the `System.Audit` privilege on `/access/users` or must be querying their own userid. The response includes each token's `tokenid` (full auth ID in `user@realm!tokenname` format), enabled state, and expiry — note that `token-name` alone is not a unique identifier; always use `tokenid` when referencing a specific token in subsequent calls.

examples.summary: List all API tokens for a local admin user

tips: The `tokenid` field uses the full `user@realm!tokenname` format required by PDM API auth headers — copy it directly when constructing `PDMAPIToken=` credentials.
A token with `enable: false` will be rejected at auth time even if the secret is valid; check this field when troubleshooting 401s.
Tokens with `expire: 0` never expire — flag these during security audits.
This endpoint does NOT return the token secret; secrets are only available at token creation time.
